title: vehicle-sil timeline (vehicle_sil_launch run --scenario --timeline), format 1
description: What a scenario did over the virtual time of one run: its steps, the values it wrote and the values it saw. Written by vehicle_sil_launch, read by tools that draw or compare a run. Every time is in milliseconds of virtual time and may have a fraction. A variable is named "<participant>.<name>" everywhere. A reader ignores keys it does not know, and does not draw (but names) a series, a watch or a step whose source, encoding, mode, op, kind or status it does not know: this schema therefore lists the values written today in the descriptions and does not close them, and allows more keys everywhere. The manual is docs/simulation-run.md of vehicle-sil.

vehicle_sil.description: The version of vehicle-sil that wrote the file.

stage.description: What the file is of: "run", a run that took place.

file.description: The simulation configuration, as it was named on the command line.

variant.description: The variant of the configuration that ran; null for a configuration without variants.

params.description: The scenario's parameters with the values in effect, as in `check --json`.

value.description: Its value, as a scenario reads it.

from.description: Where the value comes from (the scenario, the configuration, the command line).

tick_ms.description: The step of the launcher's controller: how often the scenario's engine looked at the samples and sent writes.

scenario.description: The scenario and its result, as in `run --json`, and up to when the series go.

file.description: The scenario file, as it was named on the command line.

name.description: The scenario's name; null without one.

status.description: "passed", "failed", "incomplete" (the simulation ended for another reason) or "not_run" (the simulation did not start).

over_at_ms.description: The step of the controller at which the scenario was over; null if it was not (incomplete, not_run).

recorded_to_ms.description: The time that decided the scenario, and the right end of the series: no point is later. Failed: the at_ms of the failed step. Passed: the latest at_ms of its steps. Incomplete: the time of the last sample that was looked at. null if the scenario did not begin.

variables.description: The variables the scenario uses, in the order of their first use.

name.description: "<participant>.<name>": how every other part of the file names the variable.

participant.description: The participant that has the variable.

causality.description: "input", "output" or "parameter"; null if the participant's description is not known.

min.description: The least value it takes, if it says one.

max.description: The greatest value it takes, if it says one.

value.description: The value that stands for it in the series.

ecu_step_ms.description: The step of its ECU (not the step of the variable's values).

written.description: A step of the scenario writes it: it has a series with the source "written".

watched.description: A condition of the scenario reads it: it has a series with the source "sampled".

steps.description: The steps, in the order of the file: the keys of `run --json`'s scenario.steps[], and watch and failed.

index.description: From 1, in the order of the file.

line.description: Its line in the scenario file.

text.description: What it does, in one line, for people.

start_ms.description: Its time; null if the scenario was over before it.

at_ms.description: The time that decided it; null if it was not decided.

end_ms.description: From where the next step counts; null if that is not known.

code.description: failed, skipped: the code of its finding.

expect_skipped.description: A ramp or a wave whose expect is not checked in this configuration: why.

watch.description: The conditions the step looks at and when; null for a step without conditions.

mode.description: "at": the values at from_ms (until_ms is null). "always": at from_ms and at every sample until until_ms (hold_for_ms). "once": at from_ms or at some sample until until_ms (within_ms, wait_until; when it became true is the step's at_ms). "during": at every sample of a time from from_ms to until_ms, and no value from before (the expect beside a ramp or a wave; until_ms is the ECU step that applies the end value, which may be later than the step's end_ms).

from_ms.description: Where the watch begins: the step's time. null if the scenario did not get to the step.

until_ms.description: Where the watch ends; null for the mode "at", and if the scenario did not get to the step.

conditions.description: One per variable: all must be true.

compare.description: The comparisons of its value: all must be true.

value.description: What the value is compared with.

failed.description: A failed step: what failed, as numbers (message says the same for people); null for any other step.

at_ms.description: The time of the failure: the sample that broke a condition, the time a wait ran out, the time of the write.

code.description: The code of the finding (scenario-failed, scenario-timeout, scenario-write, scenario-out-of-time).

conditions.description: The conditions that were not met (all of them, as the message joins them).

value.description: The value the variable had; null if it had none (no sample, or none in the time of a "during" watch).

sample_ms.description: The time of the sample with that value; null with value.

write.description: The write that was not made or not applied; null if the step did not fail of a write.

variable.description: The variable that was to be written.

at_ms.description: The time the write was for.

value.description: The value; null if it was never worked out.

series.description: The values over the time, in the order of variables[] (of one variable the written series first). Only variables the scenario uses have series.

source.description: "written": the values the scenario sent, each with the time it was for. "sampled": the values of the ECU's samples that the scenario looked at; a sample has the value at the end of an ECU step and the time of its start, so a value holds from its point to the next.

encoding.description: "all": every value is a point (written). "changes": a point only where the written text of the value differs from the one before (sampled).

samples.description: sampled: how many samples there were up to recorded_to_ms (also those whose points a limit dropped).

first_ms.description: sampled: the time of the first sample.

last_ms.description: sampled: the time of the last sample (the last point holds until there).

not_applied_from.description: written, only if there are such points: the index in points of the first one for a time after scenario.over_at_ms: sent, and no ECU got to that time.

points.description: [t_ms, value], one per line of the file. t_ms never goes back; points of one time are in the order sent. A bool is true or false, an enum the value of its item, a real that is no number null.

findings.description: The findings of the check and of the run that are about the scenario (code scenario-...) or this file (timeline-write), as in `run --json`; and, with their code alone, those that say the run was late (control-link-late-values, behind-real-time): what such a run recorded may differ from run to run.

code.description: The fixed name of the finding.

message.description: What is wrong and what to do, for people.

limits.description: How many points the file keeps, and what went. Beyond a limit the oldest points of a series go and the newest stay. Counted are the points of samples and the written points of a ramp or a wave; the written points of a set always stay.

points_per_series.description: The most points of one series.

points_total.description: The most points of all series together; beyond it the series with the most points give first.

dropped.description: The series that lost points; empty if none did.

dropped_before_ms.description: The time of the oldest point that stayed (of a written series: of a ramp or a wave).
